title: First ionization enthalpies of the second period
body: A student plotted the first ionization enthalpies of the second period elements (in kJ mol⁻¹): Li 520, Be 899, B 801, C 1086, N 1402, O 1314, F 1681, Ne 2080. The general trend is an increase from lithium to neon, because electrons are added to the same principal quantum level while the nuclear charge increases and the shielding by the inner 1s electrons does not increase enough to compensate. However, the graph shows two dips: boron has a lower value than beryllium, and oxygen has a lower value than nitrogen, even though boron and oxygen have the greater nuclear charge in each pair. The student recalled that beryllium is 1s² 2s², boron is 1s² 2s² 2p¹, nitrogen is 1s² 2s² 2p³ and oxygen is 1s² 2s² 2p⁴.
